Take it out a portion at a time. It keeps about 6 months in a cellar, a month in a warm room. Unseal gives the plank and stone back. Draw Starter takes 1 L at most for the next barrel; take all the kraut out to drain the rest and move it.

Salts the kraut and presses it down under the cloth, the board and the stone, so its own juice rises over it as brine. The barrel is sealed and the kraut starts to sour: nothing more goes in.

Each tomato goes in as pulp: one, the oldest, or all, as many as there is room for. Kept steaming 3 hours on any stove or fire it cooks down to paste, a fifth of the pulp (10 tomatoes make two portions); 2 hours more and it scorches. Pack it into a crock, or add it to one already started. Left raw it goes off when its oldest tomato would have; cooked and not packed, it keeps about a week at room warmth.
No room, or it holds something else. A pot takes 10 tomatoes, a saucepan 4; cooked paste must be packed out first.
Needs an empty cooking pot or saucepan, or one holding tomato pulp.
